title: Quantum Observation and Gravitational Information
overview: What can a quantum observation distinguish when two states have the same gravitational-source assignment?
question: Which quantum properties remain observationally distinguishable beyond the complete Einstein-source description?
foundation: The published Schwarzschild series supplies the original scalar-field, Fock-state and gravitational-source constructions. Subsequent internal formal research constructs a finite-bank, fixed-background, spatial-circle-window-associated two-outcome quantum measurement from that field, with bounded effects, outcome probabilities and eligible conditional pure states. A particular same-Einstein-source number/coherent pair has distinguishable probabilities for one common specified observation.
limits: The result concerns the constructed fixed-background, finite-bank Fock carrier and a proper spatial-circle test window. The associated observation is not a strictly local AQFT observable or physical black-hole detector: no causal commutator theorem, detector coupling, general density-state instrument, cross-geometry transport, post-measurement stress-domain preservation or self-consistent gravitational backreaction is established. The QGCO result is internal formal research, not a published paper.
next: Determine quantitative distinguishability; prove when the complete instrument transports through matched Fock frames and physically constrained representations; then test domain-preserving conditional stress and Einstein–scalar closure.

claims.statement: In the specified original quantum model, a number-state realization and coherent realization with the same complete Einstein-source tensor give different probabilities for one common constructed yes/no effect.
claims.scope: Existence of a particular eligible test and nonzero Weyl parameter on one fixed-background finite-bank carrier; not generic state reconstruction, strict locality, or gravitationally conditioned measurement across geometries.
